Section I

Executive Summary

Osimertinib (AstraZeneca's TAGRISSO) remains the first-line standard of care for patients with EGFR-mutant (Ex19del or L858R) advanced NSCLC. Yet a majority of patients will develop acquired resistance within two to three years, and the mechanistic landscape of that resistance has matured considerably since 2024. Three signals now dominate the clinical literature and are reshaping both first- and second-line development strategy.

First, MET amplification has solidified as the single most frequent on-target bypass mechanism, occurring in approximately 13% of patients progressing on first-line osimertinib — a figure significantly higher than historical estimates. The MARIPOSA trial (amivantamab + lazertinib vs. osimertinib) demonstrated that upfront dual EGFR/MET blockade reduces the incidence of MET-driven acquired resistance from 13.1% to 3.4% at progression (P=0.002), validating the mechanism's tractability and raising the strategic question of whether to use combination therapy upfront or sequence MET-targeted therapy after osimertinib failure.

Second, the C797S tertiary mutation — a cysteine-to-serine substitution at codon 797 — emerges in 6–12% of patients on first-line osimertinib and effectively abrogates covalent binding of all approved third-generation EGFR TKIs. A wave of fourth-generation agents targeting this variant is now entering Phase 1/2 trials, creating a new competitive battleground.

Third, amivantamab-based combinations have emerged as the leading post-osimertinib platform, with CHRYSALIS-2, MARIPOSA-2, and updated PAPILLON data establishing amivantamab as active regardless of the dominant resistance mechanism. This represents a significant strategic repositioning — from a one-size-fits-all osimertinib re-challenge strategy to a biomarker-informed sequencing algorithm.

Section II

Key Findings

Synthesized from 2,400+ peer-reviewed publications and clinical trial reports, 2023–Q2 2026.

01

MET Amplification Is the Dominant On-Target Bypass Mechanism — and It Is Preventable

High Signal

MET amplification drives approximately 13% of acquired resistance events in patients receiving first-line osimertinib — higher than estimates derived from earlier biopsy-limited studies. A landmark analysis from the MARIPOSA trial, presented at WCLC 2025 and published in the Journal of Thoracic Oncology, quantified this precisely: 13.1% of patients at progression on osimertinib monotherapy harbored MET amplification, compared to only 3.4% in the amivantamab + lazertinib arm (P=0.002).

This translational dataset is significant for two reasons. First, it confirms MET bypass as the largest single druggable mechanism of acquired EGFR TKI resistance, larger than C797S, HER2 amplification, or transformation to SCLC. Second, it validates the mechanistic rationale for upfront EGFR/MET dual blockade — the combination literally suppresses the emergence of the dominant escape route.

Strategic implication:For programs developing MET inhibitors or MET-directed combination strategies, positioning post-osimertinib remains viable (since >10% of failures are MET-driven), but the MARIPOSA data will place competitive pressure on that space as amivantamab + lazertinib is adopted upfront.

Key references: Passaro et al., WCLC 2025 (IASLC abstract); Kim et al., J Thorac Oncol 2025; MARIPOSA trial (NCT04487080).

02

C797S Tertiary Mutation Opens a New Fourth-Generation EGFR TKI Race

High Signal

The C797S gatekeeper mutation — arising at the cysteine residue that osimertinib and other third-generation EGFR TKIs require for covalent binding — has emerged in 6–12% of patients treated with first-line osimertinib, a higher frequency than observed in the post-second-generation TKI setting. C797S abrogates activity of all approved EGFR TKIs when it co-occurs with the sensitizing T790M mutation (as is typical with tertiary resistance), creating a patient population with few effective options.

Multiple programs are now targeting this mutation with allosteric (non-covalent) or mutant-selective fourth-generation approaches:

  • BI 1810631 (Boehringer Ingelheim) — a non-covalent, wild-type-sparing fourth-generation EGFR TKI in Phase 1 (NCT04820023); early data published in 2024 indicate tolerability and preliminary anti-tumor activity in C797S-harboring tumors.
  • BLU-701 (Blueprint Medicines / Roche) — an allosteric EGFR inhibitor designed to be active against C797S; Phase 1/2 SYMPHONY trial ongoing (NCT05276492).
  • EAI045 + cetuximab (academic programs) — allosteric EGFR combination rationale being explored in translational models; clinical entry pending.

Strategic implication: C797S is an orphan-like space: a definable patient subgroup with no approved therapy and a growing Phase 1 competitive set. First mover with compelling Phase 2 data in 2026–2027 will have substantial partnership appeal.

Key references: Corvaja et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024 (doi: 10.1016/j.ctrv.2024.102752); Zhang et al., PMC 2025; egfrcancer.org Dec 2024 review.

03

Amivantamab + Lazertinib: MARIPOSA Overall Survival Data Reshapes First-Line Decision-Making

High Signal

The MARIPOSA trial (NCT04487080) randomized 1,074 patients with treatment-naïve EGFR-mutant (Ex19del or L858R) advanced NSCLC to amivantamab + lazertinib versus osimertinib. At the primary PFS analysis, the combination demonstrated a ~30% reduction in disease progression risk versus osimertinib (HR 0.70; P<0.001), establishing a new benchmark for first-line EGFR therapy.

Updated overall survival data presented at ELCC 2025 showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS advantage for the combination arm — the first head-to-head OS benefit over osimertinib in EGFRm NSCLC. This was accompanied by mechanistic biomarker data confirming the differential resistance profile: fewer MET amplifications, fewer acquired EGFR secondary mutations, and a higher rate of patients without detectable ctDNA at progression in the amivantamab + lazertinib arm.

The central strategic tension: The combination also carries a substantially different toxicity profile (venous thromboembolism, dermatologic toxicity, infusion reactions from the IV amivantamab), and the subcutaneous amivantamab formulation (now approved) has reduced the administration burden. Whether US prescribers shift first-line standards is now the key market uptake question for 2026.

Key references: Zhou et al., NEJM 2024; Leighl et al., ELCC 2025; AJMC MARIPOSA OS summary July 2025; PubMed 42061572.

04

Post-Osimertinib: Amivantamab + Chemotherapy Active Regardless of Resistance Mechanism

Medium Signal

The MARIPOSA-2 trial (NCT04988295) evaluated amivantamab + lazertinib + carboplatin/pemetrexed versus carboplatin/pemetrexed alone in patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib. The amivantamab-containing arm demonstrated a 38% reduction in progression risk (HR 0.62), with benefits observed across molecular resistance subtypes including MET-amplified, C797S-harboring, and resistance-mechanism-indeterminate subgroups.

Updated analyses from Cancer Network (2025) confirm that amivantamab + chemotherapy maintains efficacy regardless of the dominant osimertinib resistance mechanism detected in ctDNA — an important practical point, since a significant proportion of patients (~30–40%) have co-occurring or uncharacterized mechanisms, and mechanism-agnostic efficacy is therapeutically valuable.

Practical implication: This positions amivantamab + chemo (now FDA-approved under the brand name RYBREVANT in this post-osimertinib combination setting) as a viable second-line backbone even without resistance mechanism testing — reducing the need for mandatory re-biopsy before therapy initiation.

Key references: Passaro et al., ASCO 2024; Janku et al., cancernetwork.com 2025; MARIPOSA-2 (NCT04988295).

05

HER3-Directed ADC Patritumab Deruxtecan: Mechanism-Agnostic Activity in Post-Osimertinib Space

Medium Signal

Patritumab deruxtecan (HER3-DXd; Daiichi Sankyo / AstraZeneca) exploits the near-universal overexpression of HER3 on EGFR-mutant NSCLC cells. The HERTHENA-Lung01 trial (NCT04619004, Phase 2) enrolled 225 patients with EGFRm NSCLC who had progressed on prior EGFR TKI and platinum-based chemotherapy. The confirmed ORR was 29.8%, with a median duration of response of 6.4 months — activity observed across EGFR mutations, including uncommon variants, and regardless of prior osimertinib resistance mechanism.

HER3 protein expression, while nearly ubiquitous on IHC, was not strongly predictive of response in this dataset, suggesting that ADC delivery via the HER3 axis functions largely as a targeting mechanism for DXd payload delivery rather than requiring high-level HER3 signaling dependency.

Strategic implication: HER3-DXd provides a third-line (or later) option that is mechanism-agnostic with respect to EGFR resistance — potentially complementary to amivantamab-based strategies rather than competing directly. A Phase 3 confirmatory trial (HERTHENA-Lung02) is ongoing.

Key references: Yu et al., NEJM 2023; Planchard et al., ESMO 2024; NCT04619004.

06

Sequencing Strategy: The Upfront Combination vs. Osimertinib-Then-Salvage Debate

Emerging

The availability of both osimertinib (with a known, manageable toxicity profile and established OS benefit over earlier TKIs) and amivantamab + lazertinib (with superior PFS and OS but greater toxicity burden) as first-line options has created a genuine clinical equipoise situation. Heather Wakelee (Stanford) and other key opinion leaders discussed this in depth at WCLC 2025: the identification of resistance mechanism at progression on osimertinib — via liquid biopsy — is now regarded as essential to guide salvage selection, with MET amplification directing capmatinib or tepotinib combinations, C797S directing enrollment onto 4th-gen TKI trials, and mechanism-indeterminate cases defaulting to amivantamab + chemotherapy.

The counter-argument for upfront amivantamab + lazertinib is that it suppresses resistance mechanism emergence at the source — reducing the probability of actionable resistance entirely. The individual patient data meta-analysis presented at WCLC 2025 (comparing amivantamab + lazertinib vs. osimertinib + chemotherapy) showed that the two regimens may have similar OS outcomes when accounting for post-progression therapy, suggesting that sequencing strategy may ultimately be equivalent if executed well.

Bottom line: The field is moving toward individualized sequencing algorithms based on patient fitness, MET/C797S/HER2 baseline status, and ctDNA monitoring — a trend that underscores the strategic value of liquid biopsy platforms and biomarker-informed clinical decision support tools.

Key references: Wakelee et al., egfrcancer.org 2025; WCLC 2025 individual patient data meta-analysis; cancertherapyadvisor.com WCLC 2025 summary.

Section IV

What This Means for Your Pipeline

▸

If you have a MET inhibitor or MET-targeting bispecific

The post-osimertinib MET-amplified subgroup remains commercially viable (>10% incidence at progression), but the window is narrowing as amivantamab + lazertinib reduces MET bypass incidence upfront. Your highest-value positioning may be biomarker-selected (MET FISH/IHC high) combination data with osimertinib in patients selected for MET-amplified ctDNA at progression, with rapid pivot to Phase 2/3 partnership discussions. De-prioritize broader unselected combinations.

▸

If you are developing a fourth-generation EGFR TKI

C797S is the most compelling unmet need in the EGFR space with no approved therapy. The Phase 1 competitive set (BI 1810631, BLU-701) means differentiation will need to come from either improved potency/selectivity data, combination rationale (e.g., with EGFR/MET bispecifics), or CNS penetration. Enrollment of C797S-confirmed patients from liquid biopsy platforms should be a priority. Orphan Drug Designation is likely obtainable and strategically valuable.

▸

If you have a payload-based approach (ADC, ISAC, radiopharmaceutical) against an EGFR-pathway target

HER3-DXd's mechanism-agnostic efficacy data (29.8% ORR regardless of resistance mechanism) demonstrates that payload delivery via an EGFR-pathway surface antigen can overcome genotypically diverse resistance. The strategic question is whether your target has sufficient expression in osimertinib-resistant tissue — ideally with a validated IHC assay that predicts response. HER2 amplification as a resistance mechanism (5–8% incidence) and EGFR/MET co-amplification are the next-most-actionable non-C797S targets.

▸

If you are building a biomarker/liquid biopsy platform

The clinical literature is converging on ctDNA-based resistance mechanism profiling as the standard of care for guiding post-osimertinib therapy selection. This is a significant commercial pull for platforms that can reliably detect MET copy number, C797S allele frequency, and co-occurring bypass mutations from plasma. No single approved assay dominates this space. Partnerships with amivantamab-combination trial sponsors (J&J) or fourth-generation TKI developers represent near-term business development opportunities.

FAQ

What are the main osimertinib resistance mechanisms in EGFR-mutant NSCLC?

The brief emphasizes MET bypass amplification, EGFR C797S tertiary mutation, HER3-driven signaling, EGFR/MET co-amplification, and phenotype or lineage shifts as actionable resistance categories.

Why does C797S matter for EGFR TKI resistance?

C797S affects the cysteine residue used by covalent third-generation EGFR TKIs, making it a key mutation for fourth-generation EGFR inhibitor programs and post-osimertinib trial design.

Who should use this EGFR resistance intelligence brief?

The report is written for oncology drug-discovery, translational medicine, competitive intelligence, biomarker, and business development teams evaluating EGFR-mutant NSCLC resistance strategy.

Methodology

How Lumaris Produces This Brief

This brief is produced by Lumaris's systematic literature intelligence pipeline, which continuously ingests publications from PubMed, bioRxiv/medRxiv, ClinicalTrials.gov, ASCO/ESMO/IASLC abstract databases, and company SEC filings. The pipeline prioritizes peer-reviewed clinical trial reports, translational biomarker studies, and regulatory submissions over commentary or editorials.

For each report, Lumaris applies a structured synthesis protocol: (1) systematic query construction using MeSH terms and free-text equivalents for the primary indication and resistance mechanism universe; (2) AI-assisted screening and relevance scoring against a curated ontology of mechanistic and clinical outcome terms; (3) structured data extraction for key endpoints (ORR, PFS HR, OS HR, resistance mechanism incidence); (4) benchmarking against the prior literature body to identify signals that represent genuine novelty versus incremental updates; and (5) human expert review for clinical plausibility and strategic framing.

Coverage window: This brief covers publications and conference reports through Q2 2026 (final data cutoff: June 30, 2026). Preprints are included where they report primary trial data. Abstracts are included from ASCO, ESMO, IASLC/WCLC, and ELCC 2025–2026.

MET Amplification Is the Dominant On-Target Bypass Mechanism — and It Is Preventable

blocks.html_en: High Signal

blocks.html_en: MET amplification drives approximately 13% of acquired resistance events in patients receiving first-line osimertinib — higher than estimates derived from earlier biopsy-limited studies. A landmark analysis from the MARIPOSA trial, presented at WCLC 2025 and published in the Journal of Thoracic Oncology, quantified this precisely: 13.1% of patients at progression on osimertinib monotherapy harbored MET amplification, compared to only 3.4% in the amivantamab + lazertinib arm (P=0.002).

sentences.en: MET amplification drives approximately 13% of acquired resistance events in patients receiving first-line osimertinib — higher than estimates derived from earlier biopsy-limited studies.

blocks.html_en: This translational dataset is significant for two reasons. First, it confirms MET bypass as the largest single druggable mechanism of acquired EGFR TKI resistance, larger than C797S, HER2 amplification, or transformation to SCLC. Second, it validates the mechanistic rationale for upfront EGFR/MET dual blockade — the combination literally suppresses the emergence of the dominant escape route.

Amivantamab + Lazertinib: MARIPOSA Overall Survival Data Reshapes First-Line Decision-Making

sentences.en: Amivantamab + Lazertinib: MARIPOSA Overall Survival Data Reshapes First-Line Decision-Making

blocks.html_en: The MARIPOSA trial (NCT04487080) randomized 1,074 patients with treatment-naïve EGFR-mutant (Ex19del or L858R) advanced NSCLC to amivantamab + lazertinib versus osimertinib. At the primary PFS analysis, the combination demonstrated a ~30% reduction in disease progression risk versus osimertinib (HR 0.70; P<0.001), establishing a new benchmark for first-line EGFR therapy.

This was accompanied by mechanistic biomarker data confirming the differential resistance profile: fewer MET amplifications, fewer acquired EGFR secondary mutations, and a higher rate of patients without detectable ctDNA at progression in the amivantamab + lazertinib arm.

blocks.html_en: The availability of both osimertinib (with a known, manageable toxicity profile and established OS benefit over earlier TKIs) and amivantamab + lazertinib (with superior PFS and OS but greater toxicity burden) as first-line options has created a genuine clinical equipoise situation. Heather Wakelee (Stanford) and other key opinion leaders discussed this in depth at WCLC 2025: the identification of resistance mechanism at progression on osimertinib — via liquid biopsy — is now regarded as essential to guide salvage selection, with MET amplification directing capmatinib or tepotinib combinations, C797S directing enrollment onto 4th-gen TKI trials, and mechanism-indeterminate cases defaulting to amivantamab + chemotherapy.

blocks.html_en: The counter-argument for upfront amivantamab + lazertinib is that it suppresses resistance mechanism emergence at the source — reducing the probability of actionable resistance entirely. 第一节

执行摘要

奥希替尼（阿斯利康的 TAGRISSO）仍然是 EGFR 突变（Ex19del 或 L858R）晚期 NSCLC 患者的一线标准治疗。 然而，大多数患者会在两到三年内产生获得性耐药，而且自 2024 年以来，这种耐药的机制已经相当成熟。 目前，三个信号在临床文献中占据主导地位，并正在重塑一线和二线开发策略。

首先，MET 扩增已成为最常见的单一靶向旁路机制，约 13% 的一线奥希替尼治疗进展的患者发生这种情况，这一数字显着高于历史估计。 MARIPOSA 试验（amivantamab + lazertinib 与 osimertinib）表明，前期双重 EGFR/MET 阻断可将进展时 MET 驱动的获得性耐药的发生率从 13.1% 降低至 3.4%（P=0.002），验证了该机制的易处理性，并提出了一个战略问题：是预先使用联合治疗还是在奥希替尼失败后序贯 MET 靶向治疗。

其次，C797S 三级突变——密码子 797 处的半胱氨酸变为丝氨酸——在一线奥希替尼治疗的 6-12% 患者中出现，并有效地消除了所有已批准的第三代 EGFR TKI 的共价结合。 一批针对该变体的第四代药剂现已进入 1/2 阶段试验，创造了一个新的竞争战场。

第三，基于阿米万他单抗的组合已成为领先的后奥西替尼平台，CHRYSALIS-2、MARIPOSA-2 和更新的 PAPILLON 数据表明，无论主要耐药机制如何，阿米万他单抗均具有活性。 这代表了一次重大的战略重新定位——从一刀切的奥西替尼重新挑战策略到生物标志物通知的测序算法。

第二节

主要发现

由 2,400 多份同行评审出版物和临床试验报告综合而成，2023 年至 2026 年第二季度。

01

MET 扩增是主要的靶向旁路机制 — 并且是可以预防的

高信号

在接受一线奥希替尼治疗的患者中，MET 扩增导致约 13% 的获得性耐药事件发生——高于早期活检限制研究得出的估计值。 在 WCLC 2025 上发表并发表在《胸部肿瘤学杂志》上的 MARIPOSA 试验的一项具有里程碑意义的分析精确地量化了这一点：奥希替尼单药治疗出现进展的患者中有 13.1% 存在 MET 扩增，而阿米万他单抗 + 拉泽替尼组中只有 3.4% (P=0.002)。

该翻译数据集之所以重要有两个原因。 首先，它证实 MET 旁路是获得性 EGFR TKI 耐药的最大单一药物机制，大于 C797S、HER2 扩增或转化为 SCLC。 其次，它验证了前期 EGFR/MET 双重封锁的机制原理——这种组合确实抑制了主要逃逸途径的出现。

战略意义：对于开发 MET 抑制剂或 MET 导向的联合策略的项目，奥西替尼后定位仍然可行（因为 > 10% 的失败是 MET 驱动的），但 MARIPOSA 数据将给该领域带来竞争压力，因为预先采用阿米万他布 + 拉泽替尼。

主要参考文献：Passaro 等人，WCLC 2025（IASLC 摘要）； Kim 等人，J Thorac Oncol 2025； MARIPOSA 试验（NCT04487080）。

02

C797S 三级突变开启新的第四代 EGFR TKI 竞赛

高信号

C797S 看门人突变——产生于奥希替尼和其他第三代 EGFR TKI 共价结合所需的半胱氨酸残基——在接受一线奥希替尼治疗的患者中出现了 6-12%，比第二代 TKI 后观察到的频率更高。 当 C797S 与致敏 T790M 突变（典型的三级耐药）同时发生时，所有已批准的 EGFR TKI 的活性都会失效，从而导致患者群体几乎没有有效的选择。

现在多个项目正在通过变构（非共价）或突变体选择性第四代方法来针对这种突变：

  • BI 1810631（勃林格殷格翰）——一种非共价、保留野生型的第四代 EGFR TKI，处于第一阶段（NCT04820023）； 2024 年发表的早期数据表明了 C797S 携带肿瘤的耐受性和初步抗肿瘤活性。
  • BLU-701（Blueprint Medicines / Roche）——一种变构 EGFR 抑制剂，设计用于对抗 C797S； 1/2 期 SYMPHONY 试验正在进行中 (NCT05276492)。
  • EAI045 + 西妥昔单抗（学术项目）——正在转化模型中探索变构 EGFR 组合的基本原理；临床进入待定。

战略意义：C797S 是一个类似孤儿的空间：一个可定义的患者亚组，没有批准的治疗方法和不断增长的 1 期竞争组。 在 2026-2027 年拥有令人信服的第二阶段数据的先行者将具有巨大的合作吸引力。

主要参考文献：Corvaja 等人，Cancer Treat Rev 2024（doi：10.1016/j.ctrv.2024.102752）；张等人，PMC 2025； egfrcancer.org 2024 年 12 月审核。

03

阿米万他单抗 + Lazertinib：MARIPOSA 总体生存数据重塑一线决策

高信号

MARIPOSA 试验 (NCT04487080) 将 1,074 名初治 EGFR 突变（Ex19del 或 L858R）晚期 NSCLC 患者随机分配至阿米万他单抗 + 拉泽替尼组与奥希替尼组。 在初步 PFS 分析中，该组合与奥希替尼相比，疾病进展风险降低了约 30%（HR 0.70；P<0.001），为一线 EGFR 治疗建立了新基准。

在 ELCC 2025 上发布的更新的总生存数据显示，联合治疗组具有统计学上显着且具有临床意义的 OS 优势，这是 EGFRm NSCLC 中首次与奥希替尼相比的头对头 OS 优势。 与此同时，机械生物标志物数据证实了不同的耐药情况：阿米万他单抗 + 拉泽替尼组中 MET 扩增较少，获得性 EGFR 二次突变较少，进展时未检测到 ctDNA 的患者比例较高。

核心战略张力：该组合还具有显着不同的毒性特征（静脉血栓栓塞、皮肤毒性、静脉注射阿米万他单抗的输注反应），并且皮下注射阿米万他制剂（现已批准）减少了给药负担。 美国处方医生是否改变一线标准现在是 2026 年市场吸收的关键问题。

主要参考文献：Zhou 等人，NEJM 2024； Leighl 等人，ELCC 2025； AJMC MARIPOSA OS 摘要 2025 年 7 月；考研42061572。

04

奥希替尼后：无论耐药机制如何，阿米万他单抗 + 化疗均有效

中等信号

MARIPOSA-2 试验 (NCT04988295) 评估了阿米万他单抗 + 拉泽替尼 + 卡铂/培美曲塞与单用卡铂/培美曲塞治疗使用奥西替尼治疗进展的 EGFR 突变 NSCLC 患者的情况。 含有阿米万他单抗的组表现出进展风险降低了 38%（HR 0.62），在分子耐药亚型（包括 MET 扩增、C797S 携带和耐药机制不确定亚组）中观察到了益处。

Cancer Network (2025) 的最新分析证实，无论 ctDNA 中检测到的主要奥希替尼耐药机制如何，阿米万他单抗 + 化疗都能保持疗效——这是一个重要的实践点，因为很大一部分患者 (~30-40%) 具有同时发生或未表征的机制，并且机制不可知的疗效具有治疗价值。

实际意义：即使在没有耐药机制测试的情况下，阿米万他单抗 + 化疗（现已获得 FDA 批准，在奥西替尼后联合治疗中的商品名为 RYBREVANT）也成为可行的二线骨干药物，从而减少了治疗开始前强制重新活检的需要。

主要参考文献：Passaro 等人，ASCO 2024； Janku 等人，cancernetwork.com 2025； MARIPOSA-2 (NCT04988295)。

05

HER3 导向的 ADC Patritumab Deruxtecan：Osimertinib 后空间中机制不可知的活性

中等信号

Patritumab deruxtecan（HER3-DXd；第一三共 / 阿斯利康）利用了 EGFR 突变 NSCLC 细胞上近乎普遍的 HER3 过度表达。 HETHENA-Lung01 试验（NCT04619004，2 期）招募了 225 名 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，这些患者在既往接受 EGFR TKI 和铂类化疗后病情出现进展。 确认的 ORR 为 29.8%，中位缓解持续时间为 6.4 个月——在 EGFR 突变（包括不常见的变异）中观察到活性，且不考虑先前的奥西替尼耐药机制。

HER3 蛋白表达虽然在 IHC 上几乎无处不在，但并不能强烈预测该数据集中的反应，这表明通过 HER3 轴进行 ADC 传递很大程度上是作为 DXd 有效负载传递的靶向机制，而不是需要高水平的 HER3 信号依赖性。

战略意义：HER3-DXd 提供了一种与 EGFR 耐药机制无关的三线（或更高版本）选择——可能与基于阿米万他单抗的策略互补，而不是直接竞争。 3 期验证性试验 (HERTHENA-Lung02) 正在进行中。

主要参考文献：Yu 等人，NEJM 2023； Planchard 等人，ESMO 2024； NCT04619004。

06

测序策略：先行组合与奥希替尼然后挽救的争论

新兴

奥西替尼（具有已知的、可控制的毒性特征，并且相对于早期 TKI 具有确定的 OS 益处）和阿米万他单抗 + 拉泽替尼（具有优异的 PFS 和 OS，但毒性负担更大）作为一线选择的可用性创造了真正的临床平衡局面。 Heather Wakelee（斯坦福大学）和其他关键意见领袖在 WCLC 2025 上对此进行了深入讨论：通过液体活检确定奥西替尼进展时的耐药机制现在被认为对于指导挽救选择至关重要，MET 扩增指导卡马替尼或替泊替尼组合，C797S 指导入组第四代 TKI 试验，机制不确定的病例默认接受阿米万他布 + 化疗。

前期阿米万他单抗+拉泽替尼的反驳观点是，它从源头抑制耐药机制的出现——完全降低可操作耐药的可能性。 WCLC 2025 上提出的个体患者数据荟萃分析（比较阿米万他单抗 + 拉泽替尼与奥希替尼 + 化疗）表明，在考虑进展后治疗时，两种方案可能具有相似的 OS 结果，这表明如果执行得当，测序策略最终可能是等效的。

底线：该领域正在朝着基于患者健康状况、MET/C797S/HER2 基线状态和 ctDNA 监测的个性化测序算法发展——这一趋势强调了液体活检平台和基于生物标志物的临床决策支持工具的战略价值。

竞争说明：EGFR 耐药领域分为两个主要领域：(1) 已批准或接近批准的 MET 旁路和未选择的奥西替尼治疗后失败的领域，以强生的 amivantamab 平台和 AZ/Daiichi Sankyo 的 HER3-DXd 为主；(2) 新生的 C797S 靶向领域，其中先发者 1 期优势很重要。 新进入者需要清楚地表明其中一个立场，或者证明一种真正差异化的阻力机制假设。

第四节

这对您的管道意味着什么

▸

如果您有 MET 抑制剂或 MET 靶向双特异性药物

奥希替尼后 MET 扩增亚组在商业上仍然可行（进展时发生率 >10%），但随着阿米万他单抗 + 拉泽替尼预先降低 MET 旁路发生率，窗口正在缩小。 您的最高价值定位可能是在进展时选择进行 MET 扩增 ctDNA 的患者中选择生物标志物（MET FISH/IHC 高）与奥西替尼的组合数据，并快速转向 2/3 期合作伙伴讨论。 取消更广泛的未选择组合的优先级。

▸

如果您正在开发第四代 EGFR TKI

C797S 是 EGFR 领域最引人注目的未满足需求，目前尚未获得批准的治疗方法。 第一阶段竞争组（BI 1810631、BLU-701）意味着差异化需要来自改进的效力/选择性数据、组合原理（例如，EGFR/MET 双特异性药物）或 CNS 渗透。 应优先考虑从液体活检平台招募 C797S 确诊患者。 孤儿药资格是可能获得的并且具有战略价值。

▸

如果您有针对 EGFR 通路目标的基于有效负载的方法（ADC、ISAC、放射性药物）

HER3-DXd 的机制不可知的功效数据（无论耐药机制如何，ORR 均为 29.8%）表明，通过 EGFR 途径表面抗原进行有效负载递送可以克服基因型多样化的耐药性。 战略问题是您的靶点在奥希替尼耐药组织中是否有足够的表达——最好是通过经过验证的 IHC 检测来预测反应。 HER2 扩增作为耐药机制（发生率 5-8%）和 EGFR/MET 联合扩增是第二个最可行的非 C797S 靶点。

▸

如果您正在构建生物标记物/液体活检平台

临床文献正在将基于 ctDNA 的耐药机制分析作为指导奥西替尼治疗后选择的护理标准。 对于能够可靠地检测血浆中 MET 拷贝数、C797S 等位基因频率和同时发生的旁路突变的平台来说，这是一个重大的商业吸引力。 没有任何一种经批准的检测方法能够主导这一领域。 与阿米万他单抗联合试验申办者 (J&J) 或第四代 TKI 开发商的合作代表了近期的业务发展机会。

FAQ

EGFR 突变 NSCLC 中奥希替尼的主要耐药机制是什么？

该简报强调 MET 旁路扩增、EGFR C797S 三级突变、HER3 驱动的信号传导、EGFR/MET 共扩增以及表型或谱系转变作为可操作的耐药类别。

为什么 C797S 对 EGFR TKI 耐药很重要？

C797S 影响共价第三代 EGFR TKI 所使用的半胱氨酸残基，使其成为第四代 EGFR 抑制剂计划和奥希替尼后试验设计的关键突变。
